title: Iteration time: GPU pool scheduling, step-bench startup, JIT caches
shape: Wall time of one warm-cache D3-32 1-node step bench (r8/r16/r24, prof=1, base-4fbaa15), container start to exit, ms; plus pool GPU-min lost to failed runs
basis: MEASURED: warm D3-32 step bench wall (container start to exit), base-4fbaa15 r8/r16/r24 prof: baseline 247 s (findings 14:00), tri-1 261 s; current runs/FAST/step_d/cut-2 85 s (same-node A/B vs jw-2: medians within 0.05%)
gap_analysis: Warm D3-32 1-node step bench (3 cases, profiled) now 85 s container-to-exit (cut-2), was 247 s: imports 9 s, ModelConfig 8 s (now ~2 s less with the per-overlay modelinfos cache), dist/NCCL init 12 s, target model 2 s, drafter model 8 s (first-time vLLM/FlashInfer imports), engine init 10 s (was 51-62 s: server JIT warmups skipped, same medians), cases 17 s, exit 9 s (was 13 s+). The dominant loss campaign-wide was not startup but the extension-build thrash: model init median 864 s over 47 runs 14:00-17:00 (flashkda digest dir rebuilt per overlay), now 0.3-2.4 s; failed GPU-min 41% -> 15%. Remaining irreducible-ish: NCCL/symm-mem init 12 s, imports ~15 s, container start ~8 s.
inefficiencies: Digest-keyed torch-extension builds (flashkda 75 s, kda_conv, dcpx, dsac) embed absolute overlay source paths in build.ninja: every overlay rebuilds the shared digest dir; flashkda e9eff3bc rebuilt 23x back to back 15:25-15:53, runs queue on its lock up to 16 min (fix: fixed /k31ov mount, testing)
Triton + CUDA JIT caches on per-step tmpfs: all Triton kernels recompiled every run (fixed in wsenv.sh, measuring)
dcp_exchange torch extension rebuilt 34 s per new overlay although digest-named (fixed: shared build root)
CuTe cache keys include real tensor addresses: ~26-45 kernels/rank recompiled every start, ~27 s (owner: kernels traced with real buffers)
Engine startup runs warmups a bench does not need (serving-shape warmup 18 s, JIT warmup 10 s, prefill glue warmup): the bench's eager pass per case compiles its shapes
Backfill holds preempted 30-60 min after start; runs in flight are killed (rc 143) and the pool shrinks to 2 nodes
30 s polling + greedy first-come lock grabbing: handoff gaps, whole-node starvation, no fairness across agents (fixed: wsplan.py)
32% of busy GPU-minutes in runs exiting non-zero (preemption kills + agent bugs that a CPU-side import/config check would catch)
